items: ★ **ECG: absent discrete P waves**, variable RR intervals; document rhythm rather than pulse alone
TSH, electrolytes, renal function; transthoracic echocardiogram for ventricular function and structural disease
Intermittent symptoms → ambulatory rhythm monitoring; assess reversible triggers

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → **synchronized cardioversion**; do not delay for anticoagulation or TEE
Stable rate control: metoprolol or diltiazem; avoid diltiazem/verapamil with reduced EF
Decompensated HF: digoxin or amiodarone; preexcited AF: procainamide or cardioversion, no AV nodal blockers
Rhythm control for symptoms, early disease, or HF: cardioversion, selected antiarrhythmics, catheter ablation
★ Duration ≥48 hours/unknown: **3 weeks anticoagulation or TEE** before elective cardioversion; ≥4 weeks afterward

rows.label: Complications
items: Systemic emboli to brain, mesentery, limbs; tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy
Anticoagulant bleeding; rhythm drugs may cause proarrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Long-term anticoagulation: **CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥2 men/≥3 women**; consider one point lower
Apixaban/other DOAC preferred; mechanical valve or moderate/severe rheumatic mitral stenosis → warfarin
Weight reduction, BP/OSA treatment, limit alcohol; aspirin does not substitute for anticoagulation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atrial flutter: sawtooth atrial activity, often regular 2:1 conduction
Multifocal atrial tachycardia: ≥3 P-wave morphologies, isoelectric intervals

benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.scope: Lower urinary tract symptoms, medical therapy, urinary retention and obstructive uropathy
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.core: Aging man with hesitancy, weak stream, incomplete emptying, and nocturia from benign periurethral prostatic enlargement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, androgen exposure, family history, obesity/metabolic syndrome
Anticholinergics, opioids, and sympathomimetic decongestants can precipitate retention

rows.label: Clues
items: Storage symptoms: urgency, frequency; voiding symptoms: straining, intermittency, terminal dribbling
Smooth, symmetric enlarged prostate; size correlates imperfectly with symptom severity
★ **Painful inability to void** with palpable bladder → acute urinary retention
Renal dysfunction or bilateral hydronephrosis suggests high-pressure obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dihydrotestosterone-driven transition-zone hyperplasia + alpha-adrenergic smooth-muscle tone obstruct bladder outlet

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**, symptom score, examination; review medications and neurologic disease
Postvoid residual if incomplete emptying suspected; creatinine/renal ultrasound for obstruction or renal impairment
PSA after shared decision-making if result changes management; elevation not specific for cancer

rows.label: Tx
items: Mild, nonbothersome → observation; reduce evening fluids, caffeine, alcohol; timed voiding
★ Acute retention → **urethral catheter**, then alpha-blocker and voiding trial; suprapubic drainage if catheterization fails
★ Refractory symptoms, retention, recurrent UTIs, stones, renal impairment → **TURP or other outlet procedure**
Monitor urine output/electrolytes after relief of prolonged obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Overflow incontinence, recurrent infection, bladder stones, postrenal AKI
Postobstructive diuresis; surgery → bleeding, retrograde ejaculation, urethral stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid precipitating drugs; reassess progressive symptoms and residual volume
BPH does not transform into prostate cancer; continue independent cancer-risk discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Prostate cancer: hard asymmetric nodule
Prostatitis: tender prostate, fever; neurogenic bladder: neurologic disease, altered bladder sensation

table.title: Medication selection
rows: Large gland; reduce progression over months

benign-skin-growths.name: Benign skin growths
benign-skin-growths.scope: Seborrheic keratosis, dermatofibroma, acrochordon, lipoma, epidermoid cyst
benign-skin-growths.core: Slow-growing, stable superficial lesions usually need reassurance; morphology guides recognition, while atypical change requires tissue diagnosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging → keratoses; friction, obesity, insulin resistance → skin tags
Minor trauma may precede dermatofibroma; blocked follicular openings favor epidermoid cysts
Lipomas often sporadic or familial; multiple lesions do not automatically imply malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Most lesions asymptomatic; irritation, snagging, cosmetic concern may prompt consultation
★ **Rapid growth, ulceration, spontaneous bleeding**, fixation, or new irregular pigment → reassess diagnosis
Deep, painful, enlarging soft-tissue mass, especially >5 cm → evaluate for sarcoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Benign keratinocyte, fibrous, adipose, or follicular proliferation; no inherent need for oncologic excision
Ruptured keratin cyst → sterile inflammation; erythema alone does not prove bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical lesions → **clinical examination**; compare with surrounding skin and prior photographs
Uncertain pigmented lesion → dermoscopy and biopsy; do not destroy before excluding melanoma
Suspicious deep mass → MRI and specialist-directed biopsy; ultrasound can establish superficial cystic character

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Reassurance** for confidently benign, untroublesome lesions; treatment chosen for symptoms or cosmetic goals
Irritated keratosis/tag → cryotherapy, snip, or shave removal; dermatofibroma usually observed
Symptomatic lipoma → excision; large/deep or suspicious masses need evaluation before office removal
★ Epidermoid cyst → **complete capsule excision** after inflammation subsides; fluctuant abscess → incision/drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: Local irritation, secondary infection, cyst rupture; removal → bleeding, scar, recurrence
Premature reassurance of atypical growth can delay cancer diagnosis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Melanoma: evolving asymmetric pigmentation, irregular border, color variation
Squamous cell carcinoma: indurated, scaly or ulcerated enlarging lesion
Liposarcoma: deep progressive mass rather than small soft mobile nodule

table.title: Morphologic recognition
rows: Firm papule; dimples with lateral compression

benign-skin-growths.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatologic morphology and evaluation principles.

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.name: Catheter-related bloodstream infection
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.scope: Central line infection, organisms, line removal, prevention
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.core: Fever or rigors in a patient with an intravascular catheter, especially during infusion, raises concern for catheter-related bacteremia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long catheter dwell time, femoral placement, parenteral nutrition, immunosuppression, hemodialysis
Poor asepsis, frequent hub manipulation; tunneled devices and ports also susceptible

rows.label: Clues
items: Exit-site erythema or drainage may occur; normal insertion-site appearance does not exclude infection
★ **Hypotension, persistent bacteremia**, new murmur, or embolic signs → complicated infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Skin flora migrate externally or contaminated hubs seed intraluminal biofilm
Biofilm limits antibiotic penetration; S aureus and Candida frequently seed distant sites

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Before antibiotics: **paired peripheral and catheter blood cultures**, labelled by source
Same organism with catheter culture positive ≥2 h earlier supports catheter source
Culture removed catheter tip when infection suspected; no routine tip culture after elective removal
Repeat blood cultures to document clearance; persistent positivity → endocarditis, infected thrombus, abscess evaluation
S aureus bacteremia → echocardiography, TEE when high risk; assess metastatic foci

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sepsis → **IV vancomycin + cefepime**, adjusted to cultures and local resistance
★ **Remove line** for shock, tunnel infection, endocarditis, persistent bacteremia, S aureus, Pseudomonas, or fungi
Candida → echinocandin; MSSA → cefazolin or nafcillin; enterococcal treatment follows susceptibilities
Selected stable long-term line infections with coagulase-negative staphylococci → systemic antibiotics + antibiotic lock
Uncomplicated S aureus bacteremia: ≥14 days after clearance; endocarditis/deep infection usually requires 4–6 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Endocarditis, septic thrombophlebitis, osteomyelitis, septic emboli, shock
Unnecessary device retention → relapse; repeated placement → thrombosis and vascular injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hand hygiene, chlorhexidine skin preparation, maximal sterile barrier** during insertion
Scrub hubs, sterile dressings, daily necessity review, prompt removal of unnecessary lines
Avoid routine prophylactic systemic antibiotics or scheduled catheter replacement solely to prevent infection

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contaminated blood culture: single skin-flora isolate without corroborating cultures or illness
Infusate reaction: temporal symptoms without reproducible bacteremia
Catheter thrombosis: swelling, poor flow; cultures negative unless infected

table.title: Organism pattern
rows: Parenteral nutrition, broad antibiotics; remove catheter

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.evidence: Not checked online; established catheter-infection management principles.

complement-deficiencies.name: Complement deficiencies
complement-deficiencies.scope: Terminal (C5-C9) deficiency, early complement deficiency and SLE, C1 inhibitor deficiency
complement-deficiencies.core: Recurrent encapsulated infections, lupus-like autoimmunity, or nonurticarial angioedema can identify distinct defects in complement function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Inherited complement mutations; family history of invasive bacterial infection or episodic swelling
Acquired C1 inhibitor deficiency: lymphoproliferative/autoimmune disease; eculizumab produces functional terminal blockade

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Recurrent Neisseria** infection → suspect terminal **C5–C9 deficiency**
Early classical-pathway deficiency: photosensitive rash, arthritis, nephritis with bacterial infections
★ Angioedema **without hives or itching**: facial/laryngeal swelling, severe episodic abdominal pain

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Complement supports opsonization, immune-complex clearance, and bacterial membrane injury
C1 inhibitor loss → uncontrolled kallikrein and excess bradykinin, rather than histamine release

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CH50 and AH50** screen classical and alternative pathway function; follow with individual component levels
Suspected hereditary angioedema → low C4, C1 inhibitor antigen and function
Acquired form often has low C1q; hereditary form generally preserves C1q

rows.label: Tx
items: Invasive infection → immediate IV ceftriaxone, cultures, sepsis support
★ Bradykinin attack: **C1 inhibitor concentrate or icatibant**; secure threatened airway early
Antihistamines, epinephrine, and corticosteroids do not reliably reverse hereditary attacks
Frequent angioedema → lanadelumab or prophylactic C1 inhibitor; specialist-guided plans before procedures

rows.label: Complications
items: Meningococcal sepsis/meningitis, recurrent pneumococcal infection; autoimmune renal injury
Laryngeal obstruction; bowel-wall edema can mimic a surgical abdomen

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **MenACWY + MenB**, pneumococcal and Hib vaccination; consider antibiotic prophylaxis for recurrent infections
Family screening; avoid ACE inhibitors and estrogen with hereditary angioedema

rows.label: Mimics
items: Histaminergic angioedema: urticaria, pruritus, allergen exposure, epinephrine response
Antibody deficiency: recurrent sinopulmonary disease with reduced immunoglobulins

complement-deficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established immunology teaching.

dementia.name: Dementia
dementia.scope: Alzheimer, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal, reversible causes, normal cognitive aging vs MCI, Parkinson disease dementia
dementia.core: Acquired cognitive decline interfering with independent daily function; distinguish dementia from normal aging and mild cognitive impairment by functional consequences.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced age, family history; vascular risk factors, prior stroke, Parkinson disease
Anticholinergics, sedatives, alcohol, hearing loss, sleep apnea may worsen cognition

rows.label: Clues
items: Collateral history: missed bills/medications, getting lost, unsafe cooking or driving
Personality, language, executive, visuospatial, memory, motor symptoms help establish phenotype
Abrupt change, fluctuating attention, fever, focal deficits → evaluate acute superimposed illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alzheimer: amyloid plaques/tau tangles; Lewy/Parkinson: alpha-synuclein; vascular disease: ischemic neuronal injury
Frontotemporal degeneration affects frontal/anterior temporal networks, often before typical late-life onset

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Patient/informant history, cognition, function**; MoCA/MMSE support diagnosis, cannot establish it alone
★ **CBC, CMP, TSH, B12**, depression/medication review; HIV/syphilis testing if risk
Brain MRI or noncontrast CT → infarcts, mass, subdural, hydrocephalus; avoid routine PET as first test
Normal aging: slower retrieval with preserved independence; MCI: objective deficit without loss of independent function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Alzheimer/Lewy/Parkinson dementia → **donepezil or rivastigmine**; moderate/severe Alzheimer → add memantine
Vascular disease → BP/lipid/diabetes control, stroke prevention; frontotemporal behavioral symptoms → consider SSRI
★ Agitation → seek pain/infection, routines/redirection first; **avoid typical antipsychotics in Lewy disease**
Early biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer: specialist-selected antiamyloid drugs; baseline/serial MRI for ARIA

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration, malnutrition, wandering, caregiver burnout; antipsychotics → increased mortality
Cholinesterase inhibitors → bradycardia, syncope, GI effects; antiamyloid antibodies → edema/microhemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Driving/home safety, advance planning**, caregiver support; assess decision-specific capacity
Exercise, hearing correction, social engagement, vascular risk reduction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Delirium: hours–days, impaired attention, fluctuating awareness
Depression: prominent distress, variable effort, potentially reversible cognitive deficits
Normal-pressure hydrocephalus: gait-first decline, incontinence, ventriculomegaly; tap test may predict shunt response

table.title: Phenotype clues
rows: Insidious episodic-memory decline, later multidomain deficits
Stroke-related or stepwise decline, focal findings
Early hallucinations, fluctuation, REM behavior, parkinsonism
Early disinhibition/apathy or progressive aphasia; memory spared
Established motor disease >1 year before dementia

dementia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [Alzheimer's Association diagnostic guidance 2024](https://www.alz.org/news/2024/clinical-practice-guideline-evaluation-alzheimers), [NICE dementia](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations/); established subtype teaching.

diagnostic-test-accuracy.name: Diagnostic test accuracy
diagnostic-test-accuracy.scope: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios, cut-off changes
diagnostic-test-accuracy.core: Diagnostic accuracy: classification performance against a reference standard; distinguish detection ability from the probability that a result reflects disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: TP/FP: diseased/nondiseased testing positive; FN/TN: diseased/nondiseased testing negative

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ ↑Prevalence → **↑PPV, ↓NPV**; sensitivity/specificity unchanged if disease spectrum unchanged
★ Positive above threshold: **lower cutoff → ↑sensitivity, ↓specificity**; raising cutoff reverses
LR+ >10 rules in strongly; LR− <0.1 rules out strongly

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Pretest odds = p/(1−p); **posttest odds = pretest odds × LR**
Posttest probability = odds/(1+odds); pretest 20%, LR+ 4 → odds 1 → 50%
Parallel tests, either positive → ↑sensitivity; serial tests, both positive → ↑specificity

rows.label: Compare
items: ROC: sensitivity versus 1−specificity; AUC 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Sensitive negative** helps exclude; specific positive helps confirm; neither absolute
Case-control sampling → PPV/NPV unrepresentative without population prevalence
Verification bias: reference testing only selected results → distorted accuracy

diagnostic-test-accuracy.evidence: Established statistical definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

gallstone-disease.name: Gallstone disease
gallstone-disease.scope: Biliary colic, acute cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, cholangitis, gallstone pancreatitis
gallstone-disease.core: Gallstone location determines the syndrome: transient cystic obstruction, gallbladder inflammation, common-duct obstruction/infection, or pancreatic inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, female sex, pregnancy, obesity, rapid weight loss, ileal disease/resection
Hemolysis/cirrhosis → pigment stones; critical illness/TPN → acalculous cholecystitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Postprandial RUQ/epigastric discomfort radiating to back or right shoulder; assess fever and jaundice
★ **Fever + RUQ pain + jaundice** → cholangitis; hypotension/confusion → severe infection
Pancreatitis: persistent epigastric pain radiating to back, vomiting; ALT >150 supports biliary cause

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cholesterol supersaturation or pigment precipitation creates calculi; obstruction location dictates organ injury
Infected obstructed bile ducts require drainage because antibiotics cannot reliably sterilize a closed system

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RUQ ultrasound first**; CBC, bilirubin/alkaline phosphatase, AST/ALT, lipase
Suspected cholecystitis with equivocal ultrasound → HIDA; nonvisualized gallbladder supports cystic-duct obstruction
Intermediate common-duct stone probability → MRCP or EUS; ERCP reserved primarily for treatment
★ Direct intervention: **stone seen, cholangitis, or bilirubin >4 mg/dL plus dilated duct**

rows.label: Tx
items: Analgesia, fluids, antiemetics; infection → ceftriaxone/metronidazole or piperacillin/tazobactam
★ **Cholangitis → urgent biliary drainage**, immediately after stabilization if shock; do not await antibiotic response
Poor surgical candidate with acute cholecystitis → percutaneous cholecystostomy
★ Gallstone pancreatitis → supportive care, early oral feeding; **no urgent ERCP without cholangitis/persistent obstruction**

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, gangrene, perforation, abscess, septic shock; pancreatitis → necrosis/organ failure
Cholecystoenteric fistula → gallstone ileus; imaging: bowel obstruction, pneumobilia, ectopic stone
ERCP → pancreatitis/bleeding/perforation; cholecystectomy → bile-duct injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain healthy weight; avoid rapid weight loss; selected bariatric patients → ursodiol prophylaxis
After duct clearance → cholecystectomy; after mild biliary pancreatitis → same-admission cholecystectomy
Asymptomatic uncomplicated stones → observation; no routine prophylactic surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hepatitis: marked aminotransferase elevation, no obstructing stone
PUD: burning epigastric pain, ulcer on endoscopy
Inferior MI: ischemic ECG/troponin changes, cardiovascular risk

table.title: Localizing obstruction
rows: Persistent >6 hours, Murphy sign, wall thickening
Cholestatic labs, duct stone/dilation; no infection
ERCP extraction or operative duct clearance
Inflamed gallbladder without stones; critically ill

giant-cell-arteritis.name: Giant cell arteritis
giant-cell-arteritis.scope: Giant cell arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, vision loss
giant-cell-arteritis.core: New headache with jaw claudication or visual symptoms after age 50 requires immediate glucocorticoids to prevent irreversible blindness.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, female sex, Northern European ancestry; frequently overlaps polymyalgia rheumatica
Age <50 makes this diagnosis very unlikely

rows.label: Clues
items: Scalp tenderness, abnormal temporal artery, fever, weight loss, fatigue
★ **Transient monocular loss, diplopia, or sudden painless visual loss** → ocular ischemia
PMR: bilateral shoulder/hip aching, morning stiffness >45 minutes; true muscle strength preserved

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Granulomatous inflammation of large/medium arteries → intimal proliferation and ischemic narrowing
Posterior ciliary artery involvement causes arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ESR/CRP and CBC**: inflammation, thrombocytosis, normocytic anemia support; normal markers do not fully exclude
★ **Temporal artery biopsy** confirms; skip lesions can cause false negative, so obtain adequate segment
Ultrasound halo sign useful in experienced centers; arrange testing promptly after treatment begins
Assess pulses, arm pressures, bruits; CTA/MRA for suspected aortic/branch-vessel involvement
PMR: elevated inflammatory markers, normal CK; screen all PMR patients for cranial/visual symptoms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected cranial GCA → **high-dose oral prednisone now**, before biopsy
★ Threatened or established visual loss → **IV methylprednisolone** urgently; ophthalmology consultation
Taper slowly with symptom/marker monitoring; tocilizumab can reduce steroid exposure in selected patients
Isolated PMR → lower-dose prednisone; failure to improve promptly → reconsider diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent blindness, often sequential fellow-eye involvement; stroke, aortic aneurysm/dissection
Prolonged steroids → infection, diabetes, cataracts, osteoporosis; IL-6 blockade can suppress inflammatory markers

rows.label: Prevention
items: Bone protection and fracture-risk assessment during prolonged steroids; monitor BP/glucose
Educate about recurrent visual symptoms, jaw pain, limb claudication; evaluate aorta over time

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonarteritic ischemic optic neuropathy: vascular risks, no systemic inflammatory syndrome
Myositis: objective proximal weakness, elevated CK
TMJ disease: local joint pain/clicking rather than chewing-induced ischemic fatigue

giant-cell-arteritis.evidence: Not checked online; established rheumatologic emergency and PMR management.

gonococcal-infection.name: Gonococcal infection
gonococcal-infection.scope: Urethritis/cervicitis, disseminated gonococcal infection, gonococcal arthritis, neonatal conjunctivitis
gonococcal-infection.core: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes mucosal infection and can disseminate into a dermatitis-tenosynovitis-arthritis syndrome or purulent septic arthritis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: New/multiple partners, inconsistent barriers, prior STI, younger age
Complement deficiency increases dissemination risk; neonatal exposure during vaginal delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, mucopurulent discharge, friable cervix; rectal/pharyngeal disease often asymptomatic
★ **Migratory arthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules** → disseminated infection
Neonate: copious purulent conjunctivitis 2–5 days after birth; corneal injury can progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci adhere to mucosa; antigenic variation permits recurrent infection
Ascending genital spread or bacteremia extends disease beyond initial exposure site

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT at exposed sites**: urine/vaginal, rectal, pharyngeal; test chlamydia, HIV, syphilis
Symptomatic male urethral Gram stain may show intracellular diplococci; less reliable at other sites
Dissemination: blood/synovial cultures and mucosal NAAT; negative joint culture does not exclude diagnosis
Suspected treatment failure → culture and antimicrobial susceptibility, assess reinfection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated: **ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once**; ≥150 kg → 1 g once
Chlamydia not excluded → doxycycline for 7 days; pregnancy → azithromycin instead
★ Disseminated disease → **IV/IM ceftriaxone**, hospitalization initially; drain purulent joint
Neonatal infection → systemic ceftriaxone, or cefotaxime if bilirubin/calcium concerns; topical treatment alone insufficient

rows.label: Complications
items: PID, infertility, ectopic pregnancy, epididymitis, corneal perforation
Rare endocarditis/meningitis; untreated septic arthritis damages cartilage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; abstain 7 days after treatment and until partners treated
Retest at 3 months; pharyngeal test-of-cure at 7–14 days; routine urogenital test-of-cure unnecessary
Condoms, risk-based screening; neonatal erythromycin eye ointment prevents gonococcal ophthalmia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chlamydia: similar urethritis/cervicitis, NAAT distinguishes
Reactive arthritis: sterile arthritis after infection, conjunctivitis/enthesitis
Staphylococcal arthritis: usually isolated hot joint without migratory skin-tendon syndrome

gout.name: Gout and crystal arthropathy
gout.scope: Acute gout, chronic gout and urate lowering, pseudogout (CPPD)
gout.core: Abrupt intensely painful inflammatory arthritis from crystal deposition; gout and CPPD require different long-term prevention despite similar flare management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gout: CKD, obesity, alcohol, purines/fructose, thiazide/loop diuretics, low-dose aspirin
CPPD: older age, joint injury, hyperparathyroidism, hemochromatosis, hypomagnesemia
Flares follow surgery, dehydration, illness, or changes in urate concentration

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid-onset red swollen tender joint, often overnight; fever possible
Chronic gout: tophi on ears/olecranon, erosive arthritis; recurrent flares separated by asymptomatic intervals
CPPD in younger adults → investigate associated metabolic disorders

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Crystal phagocytosis activates inflammasome/IL-1 → neutrophilic synovitis
Most hyperuricemia reflects reduced renal urate excretion rather than excessive production

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First/atypical acute monoarthritis → **arthrocentesis**, polarized microscopy, Gram stain/culture
★ **Crystals do not exclude septic arthritis**; serum urate may be normal during gout flare
Chronic imaging: punched-out defects with overhanging edges; ultrasound double-contour sign supports urate deposition

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute either crystal flare → **NSAID, colchicine, or glucocorticoid**; intraarticular steroid only after infection excluded
CKD/ulcer/anticoagulation → favor steroid; adjust colchicine for renal impairment/interactions; avoid NSAIDs in advanced CKD
★ Urate lowering: **allopurinol first-line**, including CKD; start low, titrate to serum urate <6 mg/dL
Continue urate lowering during flares; may start during treated flare; no routine asymptomatic-hyperuricemia treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Gout: destructive arthritis, uric-acid stones; CPPD: chronic degenerative/inflammatory arthropathy
Allopurinol hypersensitivity; colchicine → diarrhea/neuromyopathy
Xanthine-oxidase inhibitors + azathioprine/6-MP → severe marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Urate lowering: **tophi, joint damage, ≥2 flares/year**; first flare with CKD ≥3/stones/urate >9 → consider
Starting urate lowering → colchicine/NSAID prophylaxis 3–6 months; serial urate monitoring
Weight reduction, limit alcohol/fructose; replace thiazide with losartan when feasible; retain indicated aspirin
Before allopurinol: HLA-B*58:01 testing with Southeast Asian/African American ancestry; CPPD lacks crystal-depleting drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: positive culture, bacteremia risk; aspiration essential when uncertain
Cellulitis: superficial inflammation, less restriction of passive joint motion
RA: persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis

gout.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACR gout guideline 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10563586/), [ACR gout education 2025](https://rheumatology.org/patients/gout); CPPD established teaching.

heat-related-illness.name: Heat-related illness
heat-related-illness.scope: Heat exhaustion, classic and exertional heat stroke, malignant hyperthermia and NMS contrast
heat-related-illness.core: Heat exposure with neurologic dysfunction signals heat stroke, requiring immediate cooling before laboratory confirmation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Classic: older adults, heat waves, impaired sweating, anticholinergics, limited water access
Exertional: strenuous activity, poor acclimatization, heavy equipment, stimulant use

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Delirium, seizures, or coma** distinguish heat stroke from uncomplicated heat exhaustion
Tachycardia, hypotension, vomiting; sweating may persist despite severe heat injury
Core temperature often >40 °C; lower readings after cooling do not exclude heat stroke

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heat production exceeds dissipation → endothelial injury, systemic inflammation, cellular dysfunction
Sweat losses → hypovolemia; excessive free water intake can produce hyponatremia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Rectal temperature**; oral, axillary, and tympanic measurements may underestimate severity
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, CK, urinalysis, liver enzymes, coagulation studies; repeat for evolving injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway support, remove clothing, **rapid whole-body cooling**; do not delay for transport or tests
Exertional: cold-water immersion preferred; classic: evaporative cooling practical; stop active cooling near 39 °C
★ **IV isotonic crystalloid** for hypovolemia; benzodiazepines for seizures or shivering
Avoid antipyretics; environmental hyperthermia has no elevated hypothalamic temperature set point

rows.label: Complications
items: Rhabdomyolysis, AKI, DIC, hepatic failure, ARDS, persistent neurologic deficits
Delayed liver injury despite initial clinical improvement

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Gradual acclimatization**, scheduled rest, shade, hydration, cooling access
Avoid strenuous exercise during peak heat; monitor vulnerable adults during heat waves

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sepsis: infectious focus, fever unrelated to environmental load
Serotonin syndrome: serotonergic exposure, clonus, hyperreflexia

heat-related-illness.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency medicine teaching.

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection: fever, rash, sore throat, generalized lymphadenopathy after recent exposure
Weight loss, oral thrush, recurrent infections suggest advanced immunodeficiency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, resistance genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB testing; pregnancy assessment
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin or TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, urgent ophthalmology

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary brain lesion, fails empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; induced sputum/BAL

hypocalcemia.name: Hypocalcemia
hypocalcemia.scope: Hypoparathyroidism, vitamin D deficiency, post-thyroidectomy, hypomagnesemia
hypocalcemia.core: Low ionized calcium causes neuromuscular irritability and QT prolongation; severe symptoms require IV calcium while the cause is corrected.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thyroid/parathyroid surgery, autoimmune hypoparathyroidism, DiGeorge syndrome
Vitamin D deficiency from low intake, malabsorption, limited sun; CKD, pancreatitis, massive citrate transfusion
Severe hypomagnesemia from alcoholism, diarrhea, PPIs, diuretics; bisphosphonates/denosumab can precipitate deficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Perioral tingling, distal paresthesias, muscle cramps, carpopedal spasm
★ **Trousseau sign**: cuff-induced carpal spasm; Chvostek sign is less specific
★ Severe: **seizures, laryngospasm, arrhythmias**; ECG shows prolonged QT
Post-thyroidectomy tingling or stridor requires immediate calcium assessment rather than simple reassurance

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced extracellular calcium lowers nerve excitation threshold; myocardial repolarization is prolonged
Low magnesium impairs both PTH secretion and action, making calcium replacement alone ineffective

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ionized calcium**, Mg, phosphate, creatinine, PTH, 25-hydroxyvitamin D
Low albumin lowers total calcium, not necessarily ionized; correction formulas unreliable in critical illness
Alkalosis increases albumin binding → symptomatic low ionized calcium despite unchanged total concentration
Interpret PTH relative to calcium: normal PTH can be inappropriately low during hypocalcemia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic, severe, or ECG changes → **IV calcium gluconate with ECG monitoring**
Mild stable disease → oral calcium; nutritional vitamin D deficiency → cholecalciferol/ergocalciferol
Hypoparathyroidism or advanced CKD → **calcitriol** plus calcium; coordinate phosphate management
★ **Replace magnesium** when deficient; correct underlying cause, avoid overcorrection

rows.label: Complications
items: Tetany, seizures, ventricular arrhythmias; chronic deficiency can cause cataracts and basal ganglia calcification
Overreplacement → hypercalciuria, nephrolithiasis/nephrocalcinosis; monitor serum and urine calcium

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor calcium after neck surgery and antiresorptive treatment; ensure sufficient vitamin D/calcium intake
Chronic hypoparathyroidism: target symptom control with low-normal serum calcium, avoiding renal calcium loading

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperventilation syndrome: transient alkalosis-related ionized reduction; assess precipitating illness
Seizure disorder: no biochemical calcium explanation; pseudohypocalcemia: normal ionized level

hypocalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine teaching.

hypothyroidism.name: Hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.scope: Hashimoto thyroiditis, subclinical hypothyroidism, myxedema coma, autoimmune associations, levothyroxine dosing, TSH monitoring
hypothyroidism.core: Insufficient thyroid hormone slows metabolism, causing fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, and delayed reflex relaxation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hashimoto autoimmunity, thyroid surgery/radioiodine, iodine deficiency/excess
Lithium, amiodarone, postpartum thyroiditis; pituitary surgery/radiation or mass

rows.label: Clues
items: Weight gain, bradycardia, hoarseness, heavy menses, hyperlipidemia; hyponatremia in severe disease
★ **Hypothermia, altered mentation, hypoventilation, hypotension** → myxedema coma
Autoimmune clustering: type 1 diabetes, pernicious anemia, adrenal insufficiency, celiac disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced hormone activity lowers thermogenesis and cardiac output; glycosaminoglycan deposition produces nonpitting edema
Hashimoto: lymphocytic destruction; anti-TPO antibodies support autoimmune cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH and free T4** establish hormone deficiency and localize the level of dysfunction
Positive anti-TPO predicts progression from subclinical disease; ultrasound unnecessary without nodule/goiter concern
Recheck mild isolated TSH elevation after transient illness resolves; exclude medication interference

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Levothyroxine**; healthy young adult approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day; older/CAD start 12.5–25 mcg/day
Take fasting; separate calcium/iron; reassess TSH about 6–8 weeks after changes
Central disease: titrate using free T4; evaluate/replace cortisol before thyroid hormone
Subclinical: generally treat TSH ≥10; consider symptoms, antibodies, pregnancy at lower values
★ Myxedema: **IV levothyroxine + IV hydrocortisone**, airway support, cautious fluids/passive warming; treat trigger

rows.label: Complications
items: Dyslipidemia, infertility, pericardial effusion, neuropathy; severe disease → respiratory failure
Excess replacement → AF, angina, bone loss; rapid correction in CAD can precipitate ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Pregnancy: early **TSH monitoring**, usually increase existing replacement promptly; use pregnancy-specific targets
Monitor stable replacement at least annually; address adherence/absorption before escalating doses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Depression: mood symptoms without thyroid biochemical pattern
Euthyroid sick syndrome: acute systemic illness, often low T3; avoid routine hormone replacement

hypothyroidism.evidence: Not checked online; established thyroid replacement and endocrine emergency teaching.

infective-endocarditis.name: Infective endocarditis
infective-endocarditis.scope: Native and prosthetic valve endocarditis, Duke criteria, prophylaxis, IV drug use endocarditis, blood culture diagnostic criteria
infective-endocarditis.core: Persistent bacteremia with valve infection causes systemic emboli, valve destruction, and immune-complex injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthetic valve, prior endocarditis, congenital valve abnormality, intracardiac device
Injection drug use → tricuspid involvement; healthcare exposure, indwelling vascular access

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, new regurgitant murmur, embolic stroke, splenic infarct, hematuria
Janeway lesions painless; Osler nodes painful; splinter hemorrhages nonspecific
★ **New conduction block** → periannular abscess; right-sided disease → septic pulmonary emboli

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Endothelial injury → platelet-fibrin nidus → microbial adherence and vegetation
Immune complexes → glomerulonephritis; infected fragments disseminate through downstream circulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Three blood-culture sets before antibiotics**; separate peripheral draws unless resuscitation would be delayed
Major microbiology: **typical organism in ≥2 culture sets**, nontypical in ≥3; specialized serology/PCR also qualifies
★ **TTE → TEE** if prosthesis/high suspicion; major imaging: vegetation, abscess, perforation, new significant regurgitation
Definite clinical Duke: 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor criteria
Minor: predisposition, fever, vascular phenomena, immunologic phenomena, nondiagnostic microbiology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric **IV vancomycin + cefepime** for acutely ill/healthcare-associated cases; tailor to cultures and setting
MSSA → nafcillin/oxacillin or cefazolin; susceptible viridans streptococci → ceftriaxone
Prolonged pathogen-directed IV antibiotics; prosthetic infections need specialist regimen and early surgical evaluation
Surgery: heart failure, abscess, persistent bacteremia, fungal infection, or selected recurrent/large embolizing vegetations

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute regurgitation, heart failure, mycotic aneurysm, metastatic infection
Antibiotic nephrotoxicity, line infection; hemorrhage into embolic cerebral lesions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Dental **amoxicillin** for prosthetic valve/material, previous IE, selected cyanotic/residual CHD, transplant valvulopathy
Good oral hygiene, sterile access; no routine prophylaxis for GI/GU procedures or isolated MVP

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis: cancer/autoimmune disease, sterile cultures
Atrial myxoma: positional obstruction, intracavitary mass; vasculitis: no infected vegetation

ischemic-stroke-and-tia.name: Ischemic stroke and TIA
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.scope: TIA (including amaurosis fugax), ischemic stroke, acute management (tPA, thrombectomy), secondary prevention, risk factors
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.core: Abrupt focal neurologic loss from cerebral ischemia; transient monocular blindness localizes to the ipsilateral carotid circulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hypertension, smoking, diabetes, dyslipidemia, carotid atherosclerosis
Atrial fibrillation, recent MI, endocarditis, arterial dissection

rows.label: Clues
items: Aphasia or neglect suggests cortical involvement; crossed cranial-nerve/limb findings suggest brainstem disease
★ **Last known well** establishes treatment timing; symptom discovery time may differ
TIA: resolved deficit without acute infarction; urgent evaluation despite normal examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Thromboembolism or small-vessel occlusion → infarct core surrounded by salvageable penumbra
Reperfusion preserves threatened tissue but increases hemorrhagic transformation risk

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Fingerstick glucose + **noncontrast head CT** first; normal early CT does not exclude ischemia
CTA head/neck for large-vessel occlusion; MRI diffusion for small infarcts or diagnostic uncertainty
ECG, telemetry, carotid imaging; echocardiography for suspected cardiac emboli

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Disabling deficit, eligible ≤4.5 hours → **alteplase or tenecteplase**; imaging-selected extended windows possible
Thrombolysis: BP <185/110 before, <180/105 after; exclude bleeding and significant anticoagulant effect
★ Large-vessel occlusion → **mechanical thrombectomy**, selected cases through 24 hours; do not delay thrombolysis
No reperfusion: generally allow BP ≤220/120; oxygen for hypoxemia; swallow assessment before oral intake
Aspirin after hemorrhage excluded; after thrombolysis, wait 24 hours and repeat imaging

rows.label: Complications
items: Cerebral edema, aspiration, venous thrombosis, seizures, disability

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Minor noncardioembolic stroke/high-risk TIA → short **aspirin + clopidogrel**, then single antiplatelet
AF → oral anticoagulation with timing based on infarct/bleeding risk; high-intensity statin, BP control
Symptomatic carotid stenosis 70–99% → endarterectomy when eligible; selected 50–69% also benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypoglycemia: deficit reverses with glucose
Migraine aura: spreading positive symptoms; seizure: witnessed convulsion followed by Todd paralysis

lung-cancer.name: Lung cancer
lung-cancer.scope: Non-small cell, small cell, paraneoplastic syndromes, Pancoast, screening
lung-cancer.core: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or a suspicious lung lesion requires tissue diagnosis and staging before treatment selection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, radon, asbestos, occupational carcinogens, prior thoracic radiation; adenocarcinoma also occurs in never-smokers

rows.label: Clues
items: Recurrent focal pneumonia, hoarseness, clubbing, unexplained pleural effusion
★ **Pancoast tumor**: shoulder/ulnar-arm pain + ipsilateral Horner syndrome
SVC obstruction: facial swelling, neck-vein distention; cord compression or airway compromise requires urgent action

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bronchogenic malignant transformation → local invasion, lymphatic spread, hematogenous metastasis
Ectopic hormone production and immune cross-reactivity cause paraneoplastic syndromes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious finding → **contrast chest CT**; biopsy easiest site that establishes highest stage
Central lesion/nodes → bronchoscopy/EBUS; peripheral lesion → CT-guided biopsy; effusion → cytology
PET/CT for extracranial staging, brain MRI for selected stages/small-cell disease; pulmonary function before resection
Molecular profiling and PD-L1 guide advanced NSCLC treatment; suspicious nodes often require pathologic staging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early operable NSCLC → **surgical resection + nodal evaluation**; inoperable localized → stereotactic radiation
Locally advanced NSCLC → combined systemic treatment/radiation ± surgery in selected patients
Metastatic NSCLC → biomarker-directed agents or immunotherapy/chemotherapy
★ Small-cell → **platinum + etoposide**, stage-dependent radiation/immunotherapy; surgery rarely used

rows.label: Complications
items: Brain/bone/adrenal/liver metastases, malignant effusion, thrombosis, respiratory failure
Radiation pneumonitis; checkpoint inhibitors → immune pneumonitis/endocrinopathies

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **annual low-dose CT**, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoking or quit <15 years
Stop after 15 quit-years or limited curative candidacy; **ACS omits quit-time restriction**
Smoking cessation and radon mitigation; chest radiographs do not substitute for screening CT

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal granuloma: microbiologic evidence; PET uptake not specific for cancer
Hamartoma: fat/popcorn calcification; pneumonia: clinical/radiographic response to antibiotics

lung-cancer.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2021](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening), [ACS 2023 guideline](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3322/caac.21811); treatment: established stage-based framework.

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.name: Medical errors and patient safety
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.scope: Near miss, adverse event, error disclosure, root cause analysis, structured sign-outs and handoffs
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.core: Protect the patient first, disclose errors honestly, and redesign systems to reduce recurrence.

rows.label: Principle
items: Just culture: distinguish human error, risky shortcuts, and reckless conduct
Psychological safety enables reporting; accountability and system improvement can coexist

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Stabilize and mitigate harm**, notify supervising clinician, preserve relevant clinical information
★ Disclose facts, consequences, **apology**, treatment/prevention plans; update uncertainties
★ Report through institutional safety system; document clinical facts and disclosure in medical record

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid concealment, altered records, premature blame, or speculation about causation
Do not rely on education alone when workflow permits predictable repeated errors

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Reckless impairment/dangerous conduct → remove from unsafe duties; institutional escalation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Root cause analysis**: retrospective system investigation; identify multiple contributors
Failure mode and effects analysis: prospective hazard assessment before harm
Handoff: standardized I-PASS/SBAR, pending tasks, contingency plans, receiver synthesis/read-back

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.evidence: Not checked online; established patient-safety terminology and ethical disclosure principles.

microcytic-anemia.name: Microcytic anemia
microcytic-anemia.scope: Iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia
microcytic-anemia.core: Low hemoglobin with MCV <80 fL: distinguish depleted iron, inflammatory iron sequestration, globin underproduction, and defective heme synthesis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Menstrual/GI blood loss, pregnancy, low intake, malabsorption → iron depletion
Chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy → inflammatory anemia
Inherited hemoglobin disorders; alcohol, lead, isoniazid, myelodysplasia → disordered heme production

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnea; severe anemia → tachycardia, angina, syncope
Pica, koilonychia, restless legs suggest iron deficiency
Markedly low MCV with relatively preserved hemoglobin and high RBC count suggests thalassemia trait

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation → ↑hepcidin → ferroportin suppression, impaired absorption and iron release
Sideroblasts: mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts from impaired protoporphyrin synthesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear → ferritin**, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation; ferritin rises with inflammation
★ Ferritin **<45 ng/mL in anemia** supports iron deficiency; normal result cannot exclude during inflammation
★ Adult men/postmenopausal women with iron deficiency → **EGD + colonoscopy**; consider celiac testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis for suspected beta-thalassemia; alpha trait may require genetic testing; exposure → blood lead

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Iron deficiency → **oral ferrous sulfate**; intolerance/malabsorption or rapid replacement need → IV iron
Treat bleeding source; continue iron about 3 months beyond hemoglobin normalization; reassess nonresponse
Inflammatory anemia → treat underlying disease; selected CKD → iron ± erythropoietin
Sideroblastic: remove trigger, pyridoxine if isoniazid-related; severe thalassemia → transfusion/chelation

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency: developmental effects in children, adverse pregnancy outcomes
Repeated transfusion → iron overload, cardiac/hepatic injury; oral iron → constipation, dark stool

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate dietary iron, pregnancy supplementation, lead-exposure reduction
★ **No empiric long-term iron for thalassemia trait** without documented deficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute blood loss: initially normocytic; hemoglobin may lag volume loss
Hemolysis: reticulocytosis, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin

microcytic-anemia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA iron deficiency evaluation 2020](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/gastrointestinal-evaluation-of-iron-deficiency-anemia/); remaining hematology established teaching.

occupational-lung-disease.name: Occupational lung disease
occupational-lung-disease.scope: Silicosis, asbestosis, coal workers' pneumoconiosis, berylliosis
occupational-lung-disease.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea and interstitial lung abnormalities years after dust exposure require a detailed occupational history and exposure-specific imaging interpretation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cumulative inhaled mineral dust, inadequate respiratory protection, mining/construction/manufacturing exposures
Long latency permits disease after retirement; smoking adds obstructive disease and cancer risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dry cough, exertional breathlessness, reduced exercise capacity; examination may show crackles
Advanced disease: resting hypoxemia, cyanosis, clubbing or right-heart strain
Pleural plaques mark exposure but often do not explain substantial functional impairment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Persistent particles activate macrophages and profibrotic pathways → irreversible interstitial scarring
Beryllium triggers a delayed cellular immune response with noncaseating granulomas

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Detailed job/task history + chest imaging**; HRCT clarifies radiograph findings
PFTs often restrictive with reduced DLCO; obstructive or mixed patterns can occur
★ Beryllium suspicion → **beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test**; biopsy may show granulomas
★ Silica exposure → **TB assessment**; evaluate fever, weight loss, cavitation for active infection
New unilateral pleural effusion, nodular pleural thickening, or mass → malignancy workup, tissue diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Stop further exposure**, smoking cessation; oxygen for hypoxemia, pulmonary rehabilitation
Vaccination and prompt infection treatment; bronchodilators if coexisting airflow obstruction
Symptomatic progressive berylliosis → systemic glucocorticoids; no proven reversal of established dust fibrosis
Advanced refractory respiratory failure → lung transplant evaluation; treat TB or cancer separately

rows.label: Complications
items: Progressive massive fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, respiratory failure
Asbestos: bronchogenic carcinoma and mesothelioma; smoking synergizes lung carcinoma risk, not mesothelioma
Silicosis: TB/nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, lung cancer

rows.label: Prevention
items: Engineering dust controls, wet cutting, fitted respirators, occupational surveillance
Protect household contacts from contaminated work clothing; adherence to workplace exposure limits

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sarcoidosis: granulomas without relevant exposure; beryllium test negative
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: basal subpleural honeycombing without causative occupational history
Heart failure: congestion/effusions with cardiac dysfunction

occupational-lung-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established occupational pulmonary medicine teaching.

pancreatitis.name: Pancreatitis
pancreatitis.scope: Acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
pancreatitis.core: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with pancreatic inflammation may be acute; repeated injury produces irreversible chronic insufficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gallstones, alcohol, triglycerides >1,000 mg/dL, ERCP, hypercalcemia, medications
Chronic: prolonged alcohol/tobacco exposure, genetic disease, duct obstruction, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Severe constant pain, vomiting, tenderness, ileus; chronic disease adds steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Hypoxemia, hypotension, oliguria, persistent SIRS** → early monitored/ICU assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature intrapancreatic enzyme activation → autodigestion and systemic inflammation
Chronic fibrosis destroys acinar/islet tissue; lipase may normalize despite advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute diagnosis: **2 of 3**—typical pain, lipase ≥3× ULN, characteristic imaging
RUQ ultrasound evaluates gallstones; triglycerides, calcium, liver tests identify cause
Contrast CT for uncertain diagnosis, deterioration, or failure to improve after 48–72 hours; not routine immediately
Chronic: CT/MRCP shows calcification/duct changes; fecal elastase <200 supports exocrine insufficiency

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute: **moderate lactated Ringer resuscitation**, frequent reassessment, analgesia, electrolyte correction; avoid overload
★ **Early oral low-fat feeding** within 24–48 hours if tolerated; enteral tube feeding if unable
Biliary with cholangitis → urgent ERCP; mild gallstone disease → cholecystectomy before discharge
Sterile necrosis: no antibiotics; infected: penetrating antibiotics, delayed step-up drainage/debridement
Chronic: stop alcohol/tobacco; pancreatic enzymes, nutrition/fat-soluble vitamins, pain and diabetes management

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, AKI, shock, hypocalcemia; local necrosis, vascular thrombosis, hemorrhage
Pseudocyst after >4 weeks; infected collection, obstruction; chronic disease → pancreatic cancer and brittle diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat cause**: gallbladder removal, triglyceride control, avoid culprit drug and alcohol
Post-ERCP rectal indomethacin in eligible patients; selected pancreatic duct stenting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Perforated ulcer: rigid abdomen/free air
Mesenteric ischemia: pain-exam mismatch; MI: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern

table.title: Severity and collections
rows: Transient dysfunction ≤48 hours or local complication

pericardial-disease.name: Pericardial disease
pericardial-disease.scope: Acute pericarditis, pericardial effusion, tamponade, constrictive pericarditis
pericardial-disease.core: Pericardial inflammation, fluid accumulation, or fibrosis produces distinct chest-pain and impaired-filling syndromes; hemodynamic effect depends on accumulation rate.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Viral/idiopathic, autoimmune disease, uremia, malignancy, TB, radiation, cardiac surgery
Early post-MI inflammation or delayed immune-mediated Dressler syndrome; trauma/anticoagulation can cause hemopericardium

rows.label: Clues
items: Pericarditis: sharp pleuritic positional pain, better leaning forward; friction rub may be transient
★ Tamponade: **hypotension, elevated JVP, muffled sounds**, pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg; triad often incomplete
Constrictive disease: edema/ascites, Kussmaul sign, pericardial knock, prominent y descent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflamed surfaces cause pain; fluid or scar limits diastolic filling and stroke volume
Tamponade equalizes diastolic pressures; constriction exaggerates ventricular interdependence with respiration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pericarditis: ≥2 of **typical pain, rub, diffuse ST elevation/PR depression, new effusion**
Troponin elevation suggests myocardial involvement; CRP supports inflammation; echo assesses fluid and ventricular function
★ **Urgent bedside echo** for suspected tamponade: right-sided chamber collapse, plethoric IVC
Constrictive suspicion → echo, CT/MRI for thickening/calcification; catheterization if diagnosis remains uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tamponade → **urgent pericardiocentesis**; IV fluids bridge; avoid diuresis/positive-pressure ventilation
Purulent/traumatic effusion or recurrent difficult drainage → surgical drainage/window; antibiotics for bacterial cause
Stable effusion → treat cause, serial echo; low voltage alone never determines drainage
High-risk features → admit: fever, large effusion, immunosuppression, anticoagulation, subacute onset, NSAID failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent inflammation, arrhythmia/myocarditis, obstructive shock; procedural drainage → cardiac injury
Rapid decompression can rarely cause ventricular dysfunction; NSAIDs → GI/renal injury, colchicine → diarrhea

rows.label: Prevention
items: Colchicine course: first episode 3 months; recurrence ≥6 months; taper anti-inflammatory drugs after remission
Exercise restriction until clinical/inflammatory resolution; optimize dialysis for uremic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: STEMI: regional ST elevation with reciprocal changes; urgent coronary evaluation if uncertain
Restrictive cardiomyopathy: myocardial disease, less respiratory ventricular discordance
PE: thrombotic risk, acute RV strain

table.title: Nonemergency definitive management
rows: Ibuprofen + colchicine; aspirin preferred after MI
Selected low-dose glucocorticoid or IL-1 blockade

peripheral-artery-disease.name: Peripheral artery disease
peripheral-artery-disease.scope: Claudication, aortoiliac (Leriche) disease, critical and acute limb ischemia
peripheral-artery-disease.core: Atherosclerotic limb hypoperfusion ranges from exertional claudication to rest pain, tissue loss, or abrupt limb-threatening arterial occlusion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, age, CKD, hypertension, dyslipidemia; coronary/cerebrovascular atherosclerosis commonly coexists
AF, aneurysm, graft disease, hypercoagulability predispose acute occlusion

rows.label: Clues
items: Diminished pulses, cool shiny skin, hair loss, dependent rubor, distal nonhealing ulcers
★ **Pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia** → acute limb ischemia
Sensory/motor deficits signal threatened limb; do not await all six findings

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fixed arterial narrowing limits exercise perfusion; progressive failure reduces resting tissue oxygenation
Acute embolus/thrombus prevents collateral compensation, rapidly injuring nerves and muscle

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ABI ≤0.90** confirms PAD; 0.91–0.99 borderline; >1.40 suggests noncompressible arteries
Exertional symptoms with normal resting ABI → exercise ABI; noncompressible vessels → toe-brachial index
Duplex, CTA/MRA define anatomy when revascularization planned; urgent Doppler exam in acute ischemia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic PAD: **clopidogrel or aspirin + high-intensity statin**, smoking cessation, structured exercise
Cilostazol improves claudication; contraindicated in any heart failure
Refractory disabling claudication → revascularization; chronic limb-threatening ischemia → prompt limb-salvage evaluation
★ Acute ischemia → **IV unfractionated heparin and immediate vascular consultation**; salvageable limb → urgent reperfusion
Low bleeding risk, symptomatic/postrevascularization → low-dose rivaroxaban + aspirin; no full anticoagulation solely for PAD

rows.label: Complications
items: Gangrene, infection, amputation; MI/stroke often dominate long-term mortality
Reperfusion → compartment syndrome, hyperkalemia, rhabdomyolysis; irreversible limb may require primary amputation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Daily foot inspection**, protective footwear, diabetic foot care, BP/glucose control
Avoid thermal injury to insensate feet; antithrombotic plan after procedures based on bleeding risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Spinal stenosis: flexion relieves walking pain, pulses preserved
Venous ulcer: medial ankle, edema, pulses intact; neuropathy: sensory loss without ischemic pulse findings

table.title: Clinical stages
rows: Reproducible exercise pain relieved by rest
Buttock claudication, erectile dysfunction, weak femorals

pleural-effusion.name: Pleural effusion
pleural-effusion.scope: Transudate vs exudate (Light criteria), parapneumonic effusion, empyema, malignant effusion
pleural-effusion.core: Fluid in the pleural space causes dyspnea, dullness, and reduced breath sounds; classify by mechanism and identify infection requiring drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome; pneumonia, malignancy, pulmonary embolism, TB
Recent thoracic surgery, pancreatitis, esophageal rupture, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pleuritic pain, reduced tactile fremitus; large effusion may shift mediastinum away
Fever or persistent sepsis despite antibiotics suggests complicated parapneumonic fluid
Bloody fluid suggests malignancy, embolism, or trauma; milky fluid suggests chyle

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transudate: altered hydrostatic/oncotic pressure; exudate: increased permeability or impaired lymphatic drainage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Chest radiograph → **ultrasound-guided thoracentesis** for new unexplained, unilateral, or atypical effusion
Classic bilateral heart-failure effusions → diuresis first; sample if fever, asymmetry, or treatment failure
★ **Exudate if any Light criterion** positive; compare paired pleural and serum measurements
Pleural pH, glucose, cell differential, Gram stain/culture; cytology if cancer suspected
Diuresis can create pseudoexudate; serum–pleural albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL supports transudate

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat systemic cause; therapeutic thoracentesis for significant symptoms; avoid rapid excessive drainage
★ Pus, positive culture, or **pH ≤7.20** → chest tube plus antibiotics
Loculated infected fluid → intrapleural tPA/DNase; persistent sepsis → VATS evaluation
★ Recurrent symptomatic malignancy → **indwelling pleural catheter** or pleurodesis; trapped lung favors catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, loculation, trapped lung, respiratory compromise
Thoracentesis → pneumothorax, bleeding, reexpansion pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Heart-failure control, prompt pneumonia treatment; ultrasound guidance reduces procedural injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atelectasis: mediastinal shift toward volume loss
Consolidation: increased fremitus, bronchial breath sounds
Pneumothorax: hyperresonance rather than dullness

pleural-effusion.evidence: Not checked online; established pleural disease teaching.

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.scope: Community-acquired, hospital-acquired, ventilator-associated, aspiration, atypical pneumonia (Legionella, Mycoplasma)
pneumonia.core: Acute lower respiratory infection with a new infiltrate; severity, acquisition setting, and resistance risks determine disposition and empiric antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, COPD, age, immunosuppression; dysphagia or impaired consciousness → aspiration
HAP ≥48 hours hospitalized; VAP ≥48 hours after intubation
Prior MRSA/Pseudomonas isolation or recent hospitalization with IV antibiotics → resistant pathogens

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, cough, sputum, focal crackles; older adults may present with confusion
★ Severe: **hypoxemia, hypotension, tachypnea**, multilobar disease; ventilation or pressors → ICU
Legionella: water exposure, diarrhea, hyponatremia; Mycoplasma: young adults, dry cough, cold agglutinins

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alveolar inflammation/exudate → shunt and impaired oxygenation
Chemical aspiration pneumonitis: sterile gastric injury; rapid improvement possible without antibiotics

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CXR** first; CT if strong suspicion despite nondiagnostic radiograph
PSI supports admission decisions; severe CAP → blood/sputum cultures, Legionella urine antigen ± respiratory PCR
Low procalcitonin alone does not justify withholding initial antibiotics in radiographically confirmed bacterial CAP

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen, fluids for hypoperfusion; drain empyema; narrow antibiotics to cultures
★ Aspiration pneumonia: usual CAP coverage; **add anaerobic coverage only for abscess/empyema**
Stable nonsevere CAP: ATS 2025 permits 3–4 days; classic ≥5-day rule remains for severe disease
★ Severe noninfluenza CAP → consider **systemic corticosteroids**; nonsevere CAP → avoid routine steroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Parapneumonic effusion, empyema, abscess, bacteremia, respiratory failure, sepsis
Postinfluenza S aureus → necrotizing pneumonia; antibiotic exposure → C difficile

rows.label: Prevention
items: Influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, smoking cessation, swallowing evaluation
VAP prevention: head elevation, oral care, early liberation from ventilation

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: thrombotic risk, pleuritic pain, no infectious source
HF: bilateral edema, elevated JVP, cardiac dysfunction

table.title: Empiric adult regimens
rows: Amoxicillin/clavulanate + azithromycin; doxycycline alternative; or levofloxacin

primary-headaches.name: Primary headaches
primary-headaches.scope: Migraine, tension-type, cluster, medication-overuse headache, red flags
primary-headaches.core: Recurrent stereotyped headaches with normal neurologic examination favor a primary syndrome; a new dangerous pattern requires secondary-cause evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, sleep disruption, stress, hormonal fluctuation; alcohol triggers cluster bouts
Frequent rescue analgesic use promotes chronic daily headache

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Thunderclap, fever, papilledema, focal deficit, cancer, pregnancy/postpartum** → evaluate secondary cause
New headache after age 50, positional/Valsalva provocation, progressive change also concerning
Medication overuse: headache ≥15 days/month with sustained frequent acute-drug exposure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Migraine: trigeminovascular activation/CGRP signaling; aura reflects cortical spreading depolarization
Cluster: hypothalamic/autonomic activation; overuse sustains sensitization and rebound symptoms

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical stable primary pattern + normal exam → **no routine neuroimaging**
Thunderclap → head CT; negative with persistent SAH concern → LP or CTA
MRI for concerning nonemergent progressive patterns; fundoscopy and full neurologic examination
Overuse >3 months: triptans/opioids/combinations ≥10 days/month; acetaminophen/NSAIDs ≥15 days/month

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe migraine → **sumatriptan + naproxen**, metoclopramide for nausea; avoid triptans with ischemic vascular disease
Frequent/disabling migraine → propranolol, topiramate, or CGRP-directed prevention; avoid topiramate/valproate in pregnancy
★ Cluster attack → **100% oxygen or subcutaneous sumatriptan**; prevention with verapamil, ECG monitoring
Tension headache → acetaminophen/NSAID; recurrent chronic disease → amitriptyline, behavioral treatment
Medication overuse → withdraw culprit, start prevention; taper opioids/barbiturates rather than abrupt withdrawal

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic migraine, functional disability, status migrainosus; analgesic toxicity
Estrogen-containing contraception increases stroke concern in migraine with aura

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Regular sleep/meals, exercise, headache diary**, limit rescue-drug days
Avoid opioids for routine primary headache; identify personal rather than universal dietary triggers

rows.label: Mimics
items: GCA: age >50, jaw claudication/visual symptoms
Acute glaucoma: red painful eye, halos, high pressure; sinusitis: purulence and objective sinus findings

primary-headaches.evidence: Not checked online; established headache classification and generalist management.

raynaud-phenomenon.name: Raynaud phenomenon
raynaud-phenomenon.core: Episodic cold- or stress-triggered digital vasospasm produces reversible color changes; asymmetric painful attacks or tissue injury suggest secondary disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young women, family history; smoking, vibration tools, cold exposure
Systemic sclerosis, SLE, mixed connective tissue disease; stimulants, beta blockers, ergot derivatives

rows.label: Clues
items: Pallor → cyanosis → reactive redness; numbness or tingling; all three phases not required
★ Digital **ulcers, pitting scars, gangrene** require evaluation for secondary vasculopathy
Sclerodactyly, telangiectasia, reflux, inflammatory arthritis, rash, or dyspnea → connective tissue disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Exaggerated arteriolar smooth-muscle constriction; secondary disease adds endothelial injury and structural vasculopathy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical history + nailfold capillaroscopy**; inspect pulses and both hands
Suspected secondary disease → ANA, ESR/CRP, CBC, urinalysis; disease-specific antibodies based on findings
Suspected proximal/occlusive disease → arterial Doppler and vascular consultation
Normal inflammatory tests do not override tissue-threatening clinical findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Warm core and hands, stop nicotine and vasoconstricting drugs; **dihydropyridine CCB** for persistent symptoms
Nifedipine or amlodipine first-line; monitor headache, edema, hypotension
Refractory secondary disease → sildenafil or topical nitrate; do not combine PDE-5 inhibitor with nitrates
★ Critical ischemia → urgent admission, **IV prostacyclin**, vascular/rheumatology consultation; treat underlying disease

rows.label: Complications
items: Secondary disease → infection, ulceration, infarction, tissue loss
Primary disease rarely causes permanent damage; evolving systemic findings warrant reassessment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Layered clothing, gloves, avoid rapid temperature changes; stress management and vibration-exposure reduction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acrocyanosis: persistent painless blue hands, no discrete attacks
Erythromelalgia: burning red extremities worsened by heat
Peripheral arterial disease: persistent ischemia with diminished pulses

raynaud-phenomenon.evidence: Not checked online; established rheumatology teaching.

salivary-gland-disorders.name: Salivary gland disorders
salivary-gland-disorders.scope: Acute suppurative sialadenitis, sialolithiasis, mumps parotitis, salivary tumors
salivary-gland-disorders.core: Salivary swelling may reflect infection, obstructed flow, viral parotitis, or a neoplasm; meal association, duct drainage, and focality guide the branch.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dehydration, postoperative state, poor oral hygiene, anticholinergic drugs reduce salivary flow
Submandibular gland predisposed to stones; unvaccinated close-contact exposure favors mumps
Prior radiation and smoking increase selected salivary tumor risks; older age raises neoplasm concern

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Purulence from Stensen or Wharton duct** supports acute bacterial sialadenitis
Painful unilateral gland with fever; airway symptoms, trismus, toxic appearance → deep infection/abscess
★ **Facial weakness, fixation, rapid growth**, cervical nodes with parotid mass → malignancy warning
Dry eyes/dry mouth and recurrent bilateral swelling suggest autoimmune sicca disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis permits ascending oral bacteria; S aureus common in suppurative infection
Ductal calculus blocks secretion; mumps causes viral gland inflammation; most parotid tumors benign

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Examine oral ducts and facial nerve; **ultrasound** first for stone or focal gland lesion
Contrast CT for abscess/deep extension; culture expressed pus if present
Mumps suspicion → buccal swab RT-PCR, public health notification; serology supplements selected cases
★ Persistent solid mass → **fine-needle aspiration**, imaging and ENT assessment; avoid open diagnostic biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suppurative disease → **hydration, warm compresses, gland massage, sialogogues + amoxicillin-clavulanate**
Systemic toxicity/poor oral intake → admit, IV ampicillin-sulbactam; abscess → drainage
Obstruction → stimulate flow and remove persistent stone via sialendoscopy or selected surgery
Mumps → analgesia/hydration, isolate through 5 days after swelling onset; no antibiotic benefit
Tumor → specialist surgical excision; avoid simple enucleation of pleomorphic adenoma

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, deep neck infection, recurrent sialadenitis; parotid surgery → facial nerve injury, gustatory sweating
Mumps → orchitis, meningitis, pancreatitis, hearing loss; longstanding pleomorphic adenoma may transform

rows.label: Prevention
items: Oral hygiene, hydration, minimize xerogenic drugs; MMR vaccination for mumps prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dental abscess: focal tooth tenderness, odontogenic collection
Sjögren syndrome: chronic sicca, autoimmune features rather than acute ductal pus

table.title: Presentation patterns
rows: Older smoker; sometimes bilateral parotid masses

salivary-gland-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established salivary disease and mumps isolation teaching.

septic-arthritis.name: Septic arthritis
septic-arthritis.scope: Nongonococcal, gonococcal, prosthetic joint infection, IV drug use, empiric coverage (vancomycin + cefepime), contiguous osteomyelitis
septic-arthritis.core: Acutely painful swollen joint with restricted passive motion → urgent aspiration and drainage; delayed treatment rapidly destroys cartilage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthesis, recent surgery/injection, rheumatoid arthritis, immunosuppression, diabetes, bacteremia
IV drug use → S aureus and gram-negative risk, including Pseudomonas
Young sexually active adults → disseminated gonorrhea; adjacent ulcers/osteomyelitis → contiguous spread

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually acute monoarthritis, often knee; fever may be absent, especially in older/immunocompromised adults
★ **Severe pain with both active and passive motion**; inability to bear weight
Gonococcal dissemination: migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules; may progress to purulent monoarthritis
Prosthetic infection: persistent pain, loosening, wound drainage or sinus tract, sometimes minimal systemic illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hematogenous seeding or direct inoculation → neutrophilic enzymes damage articular cartilage
Implant biofilm limits antibiotic eradication without surgical source control

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Arthrocentesis before antibiotics** when stable: cell count/differential, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Synovial WBC >50,000/µL, neutrophil predominance supports infection; lower counts or negative Gram stain never exclude
★ **Crystals do not exclude infection**; send cultures even when gout seems likely
Blood cultures; gonococcal NAAT from exposed mucosal sites; MRI for suspected contiguous osteomyelitis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ After cultures → **IV vancomycin + cefepime** for severe disease, IV drug use, gram-negative risk
Stable low-risk adult: vancomycin ± ceftriaxone based on exposure; narrow to organism/susceptibility
Sepsis → immediate antibiotics without delaying for aspiration; large joints usually need arthroscopic washout
Persistent symptoms → repeat drainage, seek abscess/osteomyelitis; mobilize after infection controlled

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible joint destruction, avascular necrosis, osteomyelitis, bacteremia, sepsis
Prolonged antibiotics → renal injury, line complications, C difficile; prolonged immobility → stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sterile procedures, treat skin infections, injection-harm reduction
Gonorrhea: treat partners, screen other STIs, abstain until treatment completed and partners treated

rows.label: Mimics
items: Crystal arthritis: polarized crystals; infection still possible concurrently
Bursitis: localized periarticular swelling, passive joint motion relatively preserved
Reactive arthritis: sterile inflammatory arthritis after GI/GU infection

table.title: Special treatment branches
rows: Debridement, implant retention, prolonged pathogen-directed antibiotics

shock.name: Shock
shock.scope: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors
shock.core: Circulatory failure causing tissue hypoperfusion; normal blood pressure does not exclude early shock.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemorrhage, GI losses, MI, infection, allergen exposure, spinal injury, thromboembolism
Recent surgery, immunosuppression, indwelling devices increase occult infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, altered mentation, oliguria, cool mottled skin; distributive forms may initially feel warm
★ **Anaphylaxis**: rapid airway swelling, wheezing, hypotension; skin findings may be absent
Neurogenic: hypotension with **bradycardia**, warm skin after spinal cord injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen delivery falls below demand → anaerobic metabolism, lactate accumulation
Distributive vasodilation → relative hypovolemia despite normal total body fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside ultrasound**: cardiac function, pericardial fluid, RV dilation, lung sliding, volume assessment
Serial lactate, capillary refill, urine output; CBC, chemistry, ECG, troponin; cultures if infection suspected
Septic shock: vasopressors for MAP ≥65 plus lactate >2 despite volume resuscitation

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway/oxygen, IV access; **balanced crystalloid**, dynamic fluid-response reassessment; restrict with pulmonary congestion
